plan: This is a first-price sealed-bid auction where the winner pays the second-highest bid. This is commonly known as a Vickrey auction or a second-price sealed-bid auction. In such auctions, the dominant strategy for a bidder is to bid their true value. Bidding below your value risks losing an item you would have profited from. Bidding above your value risks winning an item and paying more than it's worth to you. Therefore, I will bid my true value of $24.

My value is $9. In a second-price auction, bidding my true value is a dominant strategy, meaning it maximizes my expected profit regardless of what other bidders do. This is because bidding below my value risks losing to a bid I would have been happy to beat, and bidding above my value risks winning and paying more than the item is worth to me. Since this is the first round and there's no history, I'll stick to the dominant strategy.
